claim.quote: Here we report the detection by the IceCube neutrino observatory of a cascade of high-energy particles (a particle shower) consistent with being created at the Glashow resonance.

date.note: arXiv submission date of the posted version. Published as Nature 591, 220-224 (2021); the arXiv posting followed publication.

key_value.quote: A shower with an energy of $6.05 \pm 0.72$ PeV (determined from Cherenkov radiation in the Antarctic Ice Sheet) was measured.

name: Detection of a particle shower at the Glashow resonance

significance.note: The abstract states no significance for the single-event detection; the collaboration's wording is “consistent with being created at the Glashow resonance” and “the evidence of the Glashow resonance suggests”.

summary.plain: IceCube caught a single enormous burst of light in the ice with an energy of about six thousand trillion electronvolts — matching a long-predicted reaction between a cosmic antineutrino and an electron.
summary.technical: A cascade of 6.05 ± 0.72 PeV reconstructed energy, with secondary-muon features indicating hadronic decay of a resonant W⁻ boson, consistent with the Glashow resonance at 6.3 PeV antineutrino energy. Implies electron antineutrinos in the astrophysical flux.

title: Detection of a particle shower at the Glashow resonance with IceCube
why_it_matters: First candidate observation of the Glashow resonance, a 60-year-old Standard Model prediction, and a way to distinguish neutrinos from antineutrinos in astrophysical fluxes.
